These are research questions; no project results are asserted here.</p><h2>Oceanographic conditions</h2><p>Coordinated sampling and environmental observations provide the context for examining associations between <i>Vibrio</i> dynamics and changing ocean conditions. Sampling comparisons will account for seasonality, local conditions and geographical differences in exposure to ENSO.</p><h2>Marine microbial communities and functioning</h2><p>Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of <i>Vibrio</i> isolates are considered alongside changes in microbial community composition, diversity and nutrient-cycling potential. Gene abundance alone does not establish activity or an ecosystem process rate.</p><h2>Coordinated observations</h2><p>The supplied project description specifies monthly sampling, increasing to fortnightly sampling as the El Niño front arrives. Seawater microbes, phytoplankton and zooplankton are considered alongside environmental measurements.</p><h2>Interpretation and data release</h2><p>Detection of a potentially pathogenic lineage does not by itself establish viability, disease occurrence or health risk. Scientific datasets will be published only after review and authorization by the contributing partners.</p></section></div><footer class="site-footer"><div><strong>GLOBE</strong><p><i>Vibrio</i> dynamics and ocean microbiome research.<br>International collaboration across a changing ocean.</p></div><p>Project scope: 29 coastal stations · 23 countries<br><a href="../pages/resources.html">Sources & resources</a> · <a href="../pages/privacy.html">Privacy & data use</a><br>Website release candidate · Project content pending coordinator approval</p></footer><script src="../assets/js/site.js"></script>
